publication_gate: A receipt becomes public only after human review, static-content serialization, release validation, and a Git commit. Database state cannot publish directly.

receipt_types.name: Change Note
receipt_types.use_when: Reviewed evidence materially changes a public record without correcting an error.
receipt_types.required_effect: Name the prior state, current state, evidence boundary, affected records, and reversible publication action.

receipt_types.name: Watch Note
receipt_types.use_when: A source check changes the watch posture or next artifact but does not yet support a public-record state change.
receipt_types.required_effect: Name the checked source, new watch condition, exact next artifact, and next check date.

receipt_types.name: Correction
receipt_types.use_when: A reviewed public claim, date, identity, denominator, or interpretation is inaccurate.
receipt_types.required_effect: Preserve the prior claim, corrected claim, evidence, affected surfaces, and correction date.

receipt_types.name: No Material Change
receipt_types.use_when: A bounded source check finds no artifact that satisfies the exact publication gate.
receipt_types.required_effect: Identify the pages or artifacts reviewed, state what remains missing, retain the prior record state, and set the next check date without claiming nonexistence.

receipts.prior_state: The DARPA result signal was In Review pending an official measured-results artifact.
receipts.current_state: The signal remains In Review; the source profile now records the August 11 canonical-page check.
receipts.bounded_finding: The canonical DARPA challenge page links an event guide and scoreboard surface, but the reviewed DARPA page does not publish a final results table, winner, measured scores, or prize decisions.
receipts.evidence_boundary: This decision is limited to the canonical DARPA challenge page and official DARPA surfaces reviewed on August 11. It does not establish that results do not exist, were not announced, or will not be published.
receipts.publication_effect: Publish the dated no-material-change receipt and source freshness update; do not promote, duplicate, correct, archive, or close the signal.

receipts.prior_state: The DARPA Lift Challenge signal was In Review at the named-performer and dated-field-trial stage pending an official measured-results artifact.
receipts.current_state: The signal is Published at the official measured competition-result and prize-decision stage.
receipts.bounded_finding: DARPA's August 11 official results identify AVIDrone at 3.84:1, MTech Operations at 3.64:1, and Xtreme Aerial Concepts at 3.45:1 in the objective category and publish the objective and subjective prize decisions.
receipts.evidence_boundary: The result establishes official competition measurements, winners, and prizes. It does not establish achievement of the 4:1 objective, certified service, production scale, recurring operation, military or commercial deployment, or a comparable operating outcome; it cannot transfer to the Waymo California named file.
receipts.publication_effect: Promote the existing DARPA signal to Published at the measured-result stage and propagate the bounded result through its assigned reader surfaces without creating a new source, signal, named-file event, score, ranking, or operating-outcome claim.

receipts.prior_state: The Shuttle Landing Facility licence signal was In Review because the public FAA record displayed January 15, 2026 as the expiration date without a later formal disposition.
receipts.current_state: The signal and Space Coast named file remain In Review and unchanged; the August 15 source check is recorded as a bounded dated hold.
receipts.bounded_finding: The FAA Shuttle Landing Facility page, June 15 spaceport inventory, and linked LRSO 18-018 licence reviewed on August 15 still display the January 15, 2026 expiration or the 2021 revision and do not supply a later formal renewal, replacement, lapse, surrender, or other disposition.
receipts.evidence_boundary: The checked FAA surfaces do not establish that a disposition does not exist. NASA facility management, infrastructure, environmental review, operator applications, missions, and utilization cannot substitute for the formal site-licence disposition.
receipts.publication_effect: Publish the dated no-material-change receipt, retain the signal and named file at their prior stages, and set a bounded recheck without inferring renewal, lapse, current authorization, operation, closure, or utilization.

receipts.prior_state: ConnectLA’s June 11 grant-agreement record described planned Starlink access for 10,635 eligible locations in more than 50 parishes by the end of summer; the adoption signal remained In Review pending observed installations or subscriptions for a fixed eligible-location cohort with a dated period and disclosed method.
receipts.current_state: The adoption signal remains In Review. The September 1 review confirms the award baseline and identifies adjacent Pecan Island planned-service and affordability details, but no reviewed official surface supplies a compatible observed installation or subscription result for the fixed Louisiana BEAD cohort.
receipts.bounded_finding: ConnectLA’s current official surfaces continue to establish planned access for 10,635 locations. Adjacent official material describes a 270-home-and-business Pecan Island plan and a Vermilion Parish discount; none reports actual installations, subscriptions, take-up, an observation period, or a compatible cohort method.
receipts.evidence_boundary: This receipt is limited to the official public surfaces reviewed on September 1. It does not establish that a qualifying artifact does not exist, that no household subscribed, or that the program succeeded or failed. Planned coverage, an affordability offer, availability, and provider-wide subscriber totals cannot substitute for observed Louisiana BEAD-cohort adoption.
receipts.publication_effect: Publish a dated No Material Change decision, retain the signal In Review, append the bounded finding to the assigned reader surfaces, and keep Git-backed release validation separate from the evidence decision.
receipts.exact_next_artifact: A ConnectLA- or SpaceX-issued project return that fixes the eligible-location cohort and reports actual installations, subscriptions, or service taken with observation period and method.
receipts.next_check_boundary: The September 8 date is a bounded public-surface recheck after the draft template’s August reporting interval. The template does not prove the executed SpaceX terms, report delivery, or public availability.

receipts.prior_state: The September 1 No Material Change receipt closed the one Louisiana Starlink Cycle 001 gate while retaining the adoption signal In Review and scheduling a bounded September 8 companion recheck. The planned cohort remained 10,635 locations and no compatible observed adoption numerator had been published on the reviewed official surfaces.
receipts.current_state: The September 8 companion recheck preserves the September 1 cycle decision and keeps the signal In Review. Current ConnectLA and Starlink or SpaceX surfaces fix planned cohort identities and expose prospective access, offer, authorization, provider-wide, and availability context, but do not supply a compatible observed installation, subscription, or service-taken result for the Louisiana BEAD cohort.
receipts.bounded_finding: ConnectLA's final-proposal files identify SpaceX and map exactly 10,635 unique location IDs across 87 projects, while current ConnectLA releases describe planned access and a 270-location Pecan Island subset. Starlink's current public surfaces supply offer, availability, and provider-wide context. None of the bounded official surfaces reports actual Louisiana BEAD installations, subscriptions, service taken, an observation period, or a disclosed cohort method.
receipts.data_quality_note: Exhibit B project descriptions sum to 10,636 because CM61-BEAD-LA-351-3003 describes 2,937 locations while location-level Exhibit C maps 2,936 to that project. Exhibit C and the issuer's June 11 release both support the 10,635 planned-location denominator. The mismatch is preserved and does not establish an adoption outcome.
receipts.evidence_boundary: This companion receipt is limited to the official public surfaces reviewed on September 8. It does not establish that a qualifying artifact does not exist, that no eligible location installed or subscribed, or that the program succeeded or failed. A planned denominator, prospective connection statement, discount, availability map, authorization milestone, or provider-wide customer total cannot substitute for observed Louisiana BEAD-cohort adoption.
receipts.publication_effect: Publish this append-only companion receipt and its bounded No Material Change result through the assigned source, signal, dossier, pathway, dependency-map, desk, envelope, and update surfaces. Preserve the September 1 cycle receipt and three-of-thirteen completed-decision count, advance no Phase 61 file or Phase 64 cell, and keep Git-backed release Held.
receipts.exact_next_artifact: A ConnectLA- or SpaceX-issued project return that fixes the eligible-location cohort and reports actual installations, subscriptions, or service taken with observation period and method.
receipts.next_check_trigger: Reopen earlier if ConnectLA, SpaceX, or Starlink publishes the exact fixed-cohort outcome return; otherwise reconcile this hold in the October 9 Evidence Cycle 001 final audit.
receipts.next_check_boundary: October 9 is the existing Cycle 001 final-audit date, not a new or fourteenth gate. An earlier issuer return may trigger review, but no outcome may be inferred or predated.
